title: Visit Babylon, Iraq: complete guide to the ruins (2026)
h1: Babylon, Iraq: a complete guide to visiting Nebuchadnezzar's city
description: How to visit Babylon in Iraq: history, the Ishtar Gate, the Lion of Babylon, the Processional Way, getting there from Baghdad and a local guide's tips.
excerpt: The Ishtar Gate foundations, the Lion of Babylon and the Processional Way: what to see, how to get there from Baghdad and when to go.
keywords: visit Babylon Iraq, Babylon ruins, Babylon day trip from Baghdad, Ishtar Gate, Lion of Babylon, Nebuchadnezzar, Hanging Gardens of Babylon, Babylon tour
image_alt: A visitor walks between the ancient brick walls of Babylon near Hilla, Iraq
facts: Babil Province, near Hilla, about 85 km south of Baghdad
faq: How far is Babylon from Baghdad?
About 85 km south. The drive takes around an hour and a half, depending on traffic and checkpoints.
Can I visit Babylon as a day trip from Baghdad?
Yes. The site takes two to three hours to explore, so a day trip from Baghdad is the most common way to visit.
Is the original Ishtar Gate in Babylon?
The famous glazed section was rebuilt in Berlin's Pergamon Museum. Babylon has a smaller replica at the entrance and the original foundations of the gate, with bull and dragon reliefs still in place.
Do the Hanging Gardens of Babylon still exist?
No, and no firm archaeological evidence for them has been found at Babylon. Some scholars think they may have stood in another city, possibly Nineveh.
When is the best time to visit Babylon?
October to April, when the weather is mild. Summer temperatures often pass 45 °C, so in those months visit early in the morning.
Do I need a visa to visit Iraq?
Entry rules change from time to time. Check the latest official information for your nationality before booking your trip.

title: Imam Ali Shrine, Najaf: visitor guide & etiquette
h1: The Imam Ali Shrine in Najaf: history, what to see and how to visit
description: Visit the Imam Ali Shrine in Najaf, Iraq: its history, the golden dome and courtyard, getting there from Baghdad, dress code and a local guide's tips.
excerpt: The golden dome, the Clock Gate and the great courtyard: history, etiquette and how to reach Najaf from Baghdad.
keywords: Imam Ali Shrine Najaf, visit Najaf Iraq, Najaf golden dome, Imam Ali holy shrine, Najaf from Baghdad, Kufa and Najaf tour, Wadi al-Salam, Iraq ziyarat
image_alt: Golden domes and minarets of the Imam Ali Shrine in Najaf, Iraq
facts: Centre of Najaf, about 160 km south of Baghdad
faq: How far is Najaf from Baghdad?
About 160 km south. By car the journey usually takes two and a half to three hours.
Can non-Muslims visit the Imam Ali Shrine?
Respectful visitors are welcomed in the courtyards. Dress modestly and go with a local guide, who can explain the customs and help at the entrances.
What should I wear to visit the shrine?
Men wear long trousers and sleeves. Women cover their hair and wear a long, loose abaya; your guide can help you arrange one.
Who is buried in the Imam Ali Shrine?
Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib, cousin and son-in-law of the Prophet Muhammad. According to Shia tradition the Prophets Adam and Noah are buried here too.
When is the best time to visit Najaf?
October to April is the most comfortable season. At any time of year, the hour before sunset and the evening are the most beautiful moments in the courtyard.
Can I combine Najaf with Kufa and Karbala?
Yes. Kufa is only about 10 km away, and Najaf, Kufa and Karbala are often visited together on a heritage tour of central Iraq.

facts: Centre of Karbala, about 100 km south-west of Baghdad
Core built by 'Adud al-Dawla, c. 977–982 CE
About 27 m high, gilded in the 1790s
faq: How far is Karbala from Baghdad?
About 100 km south-west. By car the journey usually takes one and a half to two hours.
Can non-Muslims visit the Imam Hussein Shrine?
Respectful visitors are welcomed in the courtyards. Dress modestly and go with a local guide, who can explain the customs and help at the entrances.
What should I wear to visit the shrine?
Men wear long trousers and sleeves. Women cover their hair and wear a long, loose abaya; your guide can help you arrange one.
What is Bayn al-Haramayn?
It is the wide pedestrian esplanade between the Imam Hussein Shrine and the shrine of al-Abbas. Walking it at dusk is one of the highlights of Karbala.
When is the best time to visit Karbala?
October to April is the most comfortable season. Muharram and Arbaeen bring huge crowds, so check the calendar with your guide if you prefer a quiet visit.
Can I combine Karbala with Najaf and Babylon?
Yes. Najaf is about 80 km to the south and Babylon is a short drive east, so they are often visited together on a heritage tour.

title: Ishtar Gate of Babylon, Iraq: what to see today
h1: The Ishtar Gate of Babylon: history and what you can still see in Iraq
description: Visit the Ishtar Gate in Babylon, Iraq: its bulls and dragons, the journey to Berlin, the original foundations on site and tips from a local guide.
excerpt: The blue replica, the original reliefs still in place and the Processional Way: a guide to the Ishtar Gate at Babylon.
keywords: Ishtar Gate Babylon, visit Ishtar Gate Iraq, Ishtar Gate original foundations, Processional Way Babylon, Nebuchadnezzar II, mushhushshu dragon, Pergamon Museum Ishtar Gate, Babylon day trip from Baghdad

facts: Babylon, near Hilla, about 85 km south of Baghdad
Ishtar, goddess of love and war

At least 1 hour (2–3 hours for all of Babylon)
faq: Is the original Ishtar Gate in Babylon or in Berlin?
Both, in a way. The glazed front section was reconstructed in Berlin's Pergamon Museum, while the original unglazed foundations with bull and dragon reliefs remain in place at Babylon.
Is the blue gate at Babylon original?
No. The bright blue gate at the entrance of the site is a smaller modern replica. The ancient parts are the foundations a short walk away.
What animals are on the Ishtar Gate?
Bulls, sacred to the storm god Adad, and the mushhushshu dragon of Marduk. Glazed lions, the symbol of Ishtar, lined the Processional Way leading to the gate.
How far is the Ishtar Gate from Baghdad?
Babylon is about 85 km south of Baghdad, around an hour and a half by car depending on traffic.
When is the best time to visit?
October to April, when the weather is mild. In summer, visit early in the morning.
Do I need a visa to visit Iraq?
Entry rules change from time to time. Check the latest official information for your nationality before booking your trip.

h1: The Great Mosque of Kufa: history, holy stations and how to visit
description: Visit the Great Mosque of Kufa in Iraq: Imam Ali's mihrab, the stations of the prophets, Noah's Ark site, nearby shrines and tips from a local guide.
excerpt: One of the oldest mosques in the world, where Imam Ali prayed and judged: history, what to see and practical tips for Kufa.
keywords: Great Mosque of Kufa, visit Kufa mosque, Kufa Iraq, Imam Ali mihrab Kufa, Muslim ibn Aqil shrine, House of Imam Ali Kufa, Najaf and Kufa tour, Iraq ziyarat

facts: Kufa, about 10 km northeast of Najaf

Prayer place and seat of Imam Ali
Nearly square, about 110 m per side
1.5–2 hours with the House of Imam Ali
faq: Where is the Great Mosque of Kufa?
In the old centre of Kufa, on the Euphrates, about 10 km northeast of Najaf in southern-central Iraq.
Why is the Kufa mosque important?
It is one of the oldest mosques in the world and the place where Imam Ali led prayers, preached and judged while Kufa was his capital.
What are the maqams in the courtyard?
Small covered platforms marking places linked by tradition to prophets and Imams, such as Abraham, Adam, Gabriel and Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq.
Can non-Muslims visit the Great Mosque of Kufa?
Respectful visitors are generally welcomed in the courtyard with modest dress; women are usually asked to wear an abaya. Follow the guidance of the staff.
How long does a visit take?
Allow 1.5 to 2 hours including the nearby House of Imam Ali and the shrine of Muslim ibn Aqil.
Do I need a visa to visit Iraq?
Entry rules change from time to time. Check the latest official information for your nationality before booking your trip.

title: Al-Mutanabbi Street, Baghdad: book market guide
h1: Al-Mutanabbi Street in Baghdad: the book street, Friday market and Shabandar Café
description: Visit Al-Mutanabbi Street in Baghdad: history of the book street, the Friday book market, Shabandar Café, the Qishla and tips from a local guide.
excerpt: Book stalls, the Friday market, tea at Shabandar Café and the poet's statue by the Tigris: how to enjoy Baghdad's famous book street.
keywords: Al-Mutanabbi Street, Mutanabbi Street Baghdad, Baghdad book market, Shabandar Cafe, Qishla Baghdad, old Baghdad walking tour, things to do in Baghdad, Iraq tour
image_alt: Bronze statue of the poet al-Mutanabbi against a blue sky, with the Qishla clock tower and a yellow brick wall behind
facts: Old Baghdad, Rusafa side of the Tigris
faq: Where is Al-Mutanabbi Street?
In the old city of Baghdad, on the Rusafa side on the east bank of the Tigris. It branches off al-Rasheed Street and ends at the river.
When is the best time to visit Mutanabbi Street?
Friday morning, when second-hand books cover the pavements and the street is buzzing. The cooler months from October to April are the most pleasant.
Who was al-Mutanabbi?
Abu al-Tayyib al-Mutanabbi was an Abbasid-era poet, born around 915 in Kufa and died in 965, regarded as one of the greatest poets of the Arabic language.
What is Shabandar Café?
A legendary tea house from 1917 at the end of the street, a meeting place for writers and intellectuals, its walls covered with old photographs.
What else is nearby?
The Qishla and its clock tower, Souq al-Saray, al-Mustansiriya Madrasa, the Baghdadi Museum and the coppersmiths' Souq al-Safafeer are all within walking distance.
Is Mutanabbi Street part of the tour?
Yes, it is part of the Baghdad day on Fable Tour's 7-day Iraq tour, usually with tea at Shabandar Café.

title: Ziggurat of Ur, Iraq: visitor guide and history
h1: The Great Ziggurat of Ur: history, what to see and how to visit
description: Visit the Ziggurat of Ur near Nasiriyah: 4,000-year-old temple of the moon god, Royal Tombs, House of Abraham and practical tips from a local guide.
excerpt: The best-preserved ziggurat of Mesopotamia, built around 2100 BC for the moon god: history, what to see and tips for your visit.
keywords: Ziggurat of Ur, visit Ur Iraq, Great Ziggurat of Ur, Ur of the Chaldees, House of Abraham Ur, Nasiriyah, Royal Tombs of Ur, Mesopotamia tour, Iraq tour
image_alt: The Great Ziggurat of Ur, a massive brick temple platform with its front staircase, rising from the flat desert plain near Nasiriyah
facts: Tell al-Muqayyar, about 15 km southwest of Nasiriyah
At least 2 hours with the Royal Tombs
faq: Where is the Ziggurat of Ur?
At Tell al-Muqayyar in Dhi Qar province, southern Iraq, about 15 km southwest of Nasiriyah and west of the Euphrates.
Who built the Ziggurat of Ur?
King Ur-Nammu, founder of the Third Dynasty of Ur, began it around 2100 BC; his son Shulgi completed it. Nabonidus of Babylon restored it in the 6th century BC.
What was the ziggurat used for?
It was a stepped temple platform with a shrine on top, dedicated to Nanna, the moon god and patron of Ur. It was not a tomb.
Is Ur really the city of Abraham?
According to tradition, Ur of the Chaldees was the birthplace of the Prophet Abraham, and a restored house in the old quarter is known as the House of Abraham.
How do I get to Ur from Baghdad?
Nasiriyah is around 360 km south of Baghdad, roughly five hours by road, and the site is a short drive from there. Most visitors combine Ur with the Marshes and Basra.
When is the best time to visit Ur?
From October to April. Come early in the morning or late in the afternoon, when the light is soft and the bricks glow gold.

title: Malwiya minaret, Samarra: visitor guide and history
h1: The Malwiya minaret of Samarra: history, what to see and how to visit
description: Visit the Malwiya minaret in Samarra: the 52 m spiral tower of the Abbasid Great Mosque, its history, nearby sights and tips from a local guide.
excerpt: The famous spiral minaret of the Abbasid capital Samarra, built in the 9th century: history, the Great Mosque and tips for your visit.
keywords: Malwiya minaret Samarra, spiral minaret Samarra, Great Mosque of Samarra, visit Samarra Iraq, Abbasid Samarra, Abu Dulaf Mosque, Samarra Archaeological City, Iraq tour
image_alt: The Malwiya spiral minaret of Samarra, a tall coiled tower of golden brick with an outer ramp, against a clear blue sky
facts: Samarra, on the Tigris, about 125 km north of Baghdad
About 52 m, base about 33 m wide
faq: Where is the Malwiya minaret?
In Samarra, Salah al-Din province, on the east bank of the Tigris about 125 km north of Baghdad, next to the walls of the Great Mosque of Samarra.
Who built the spiral minaret of Samarra?
The Abbasid caliph al-Mutawakkil built it between 848 and 852 together with the Great Mosque, when Samarra was the capital of the caliphate.
How tall is the Malwiya?
It is about 52 metres high and roughly 33 metres wide at the base, with a spiral ramp winding around the outside up to a small pavilion at the top.
Can you climb the Malwiya minaret?
Climbing is not always permitted; access is decided on site by the staff. If it is allowed, wear good shoes, because the ramp has no railing.
How do I get to Samarra from Baghdad?
Samarra is about 125 km north of Baghdad, roughly two hours by road, and makes an easy day trip with a driver and guide.
What else can I see in Samarra?
The Great Mosque walls, the Abu Dulaf Mosque with a smaller spiral minaret, remains of the Abbasid palaces and the al-Askari shrine with its golden dome.

title: Visit Basra, Iraq: travel guide to the gateway of the south
h1: Visit Basra, Iraq: the Shatt al-Arab, old shanasheel houses and the city of Sinbad
description: Visit Basra in Iraq: the Shatt al-Arab Corniche, Basra Museum, shanasheel houses of the old city, history, best season and tips from a local guide.
excerpt: Iraq's great southern port on the Shatt al-Arab: its history, the Corniche, the Basra Museum, old shanasheel houses and travel tips.
keywords: visit Basra Iraq, Basra travel guide, Shatt al-Arab Corniche, Basra Museum, shanasheel houses Basra, things to do in Basra, Sinbad Basra, southern Iraq tour
image_alt: Sunset over the Shatt al-Arab in Basra, with date palms silhouetted against a golden and orange sky above the river
facts: Southern Iraq, on the Shatt al-Arab, about 545 km south-east of Baghdad by road
The Corniche, Basra Museum, shanasheel houses, dates
1–2 days, plus day trips to Qurna, the Marshes and Ur
faq: Where is Basra?
Basra is in the far south of Iraq on the west bank of the Shatt al-Arab, the river formed by the Tigris and Euphrates, roughly 545 km south-east of Baghdad by road.
What is Basra famous for?
For the Shatt al-Arab and its palm groves, its long history as a port and centre of learning, the tales of Sinbad the Sailor, shanasheel houses and excellent dates.
What should I see in Basra?
Walk the Corniche at sunset, visit the Basra Museum in a former palace on the river, explore the old shanasheel lanes and bazaars, and see the Armenian Church of the Holy Virgin Mary.
How do I get to Basra?
Basra International Airport has domestic flights from Baghdad and Erbil and regional connections. By road from Baghdad the trip is long, so it is best combined with stops at sites on the way.
When is the best time to visit Basra?
From late October to March. Summers in Basra are very hot, while winter days are pleasant and ideal for walking by the river.
What can I visit near Basra?
Qurna, where the Tigris and Euphrates meet, the Mesopotamian Marshes and the ancient Sumerian city of Ur are all within easy reach on day trips.

title: Visit the Mesopotamian Marshes, Iraq: Ahwar travel guide
h1: Visit the Mesopotamian Marshes of Iraq: reeds, boats and the mudhif
description: Visit the Mesopotamian Marshes in Iraq: boat trips from Chibayish, reed mudhif houses, buffalo, birds, UNESCO status, best season and local guide tips.
excerpt: The Ahwar of southern Iraq: a UNESCO-listed world of reeds, boats, buffalo and mudhif guesthouses, with tips for your visit.
keywords: visit Mesopotamian Marshes Iraq, Iraq marshes tour, Ahwar Iraq, Chibayish boat trip, mudhif reed house, Marsh Arabs, Iraq birdwatching, southern Iraq travel
image_alt: A traditional mudhif guesthouse of arched woven reeds on a small island in the Mesopotamian Marshes under a bright blue sky
facts: Southern Iraq, between Nasiriyah, Amarah and Basra
UNESCO, since 2016 (with Ur, Uruk and Eridu)
Mashoof boat trips, mudhif reed houses, water buffalo, birds
Half a day to a full day
faq: Where are the Mesopotamian Marshes?
They lie in the lowlands of southern Iraq where the Tigris and Euphrates meet, in the provinces of Dhi Qar, Maysan and Basra. Most visitors start from the town of Chibayish.
Are the Iraqi marshes a UNESCO site?
Yes. Since 2016 the Ahwar of Southern Iraq have been a World Heritage Site, listed together with the ancient cities of Ur, Uruk and Eridu.
What can I do in the marshes?
Take a boat trip in a traditional mashoof, watch birds and water buffalo, visit a mudhif reed guesthouse, see village life and taste geymar and fresh fish.
How do I get to the marshes?
Chibayish is roughly one and a half to two hours by road from Nasiriyah or Basra. The marshes combine well with a visit to Ur or to Qurna.
When is the best time to visit?
From late October to March, when days are mild and many migratory birds are present. Go early in the morning for the best light and cooler temperatures.
What is a mudhif?
A large traditional guesthouse built entirely from bundles of reeds bent into arches and covered with reed mats, used to welcome guests and hold gatherings.

title: Visit Uruk (Warka), Iraq: guide to the first city
h1: Visit Uruk (Warka) in Iraq: the first city, where writing began
description: Visit Uruk (Warka) in Iraq: the city of Gilgamesh where writing began. Eanna, the White Temple, the 9 km wall, how to get there and the best season.
excerpt: Uruk, the world's first great city: Eanna, the White Temple, Gilgamesh's walls and practical tips for your visit.
keywords: visit Uruk Iraq, Uruk Warka, first city in the world, Gilgamesh Uruk, White Temple Uruk, Eanna Inanna, where writing began, southern Iraq archaeology
image_alt: Reconstructed columns from the Eanna temple of Uruk covered in red, cream and grey clay cone mosaics in zigzag and diamond patterns
faq: Where is Uruk?
Uruk (Warka) lies in Al-Muthanna province in southern Iraq, east of Samawah and roughly 300 km south-east of Baghdad by road.
Why is Uruk called the first city?
During the Uruk period (about 4000–3100 BCE) it grew into the largest urban centre of its age, with temples, workshops and administration, and some of the earliest writing known.
Was Gilgamesh a king of Uruk?
According to the Sumerian King List he ruled Uruk, and the Epic of Gilgamesh praises the city's walls, which archaeologists have traced for about 9 km.
What can I see at Uruk today?
The Eanna precinct of Inanna with its ziggurat mound, the Anu ziggurat and the remains of the White Temple, later temples and traces of the city wall.
Is Uruk a UNESCO World Heritage Site?
Yes. Since 2016 it has been part of the Ahwar of Southern Iraq World Heritage Site, together with Ur, Eridu and the Mesopotamian Marshes.
When is the best time to visit Uruk?
From late October to March. There is no shade at the site, so summer visits should be limited to very early mornings.
